## Axial angular momentum: flux form and closure (`conserve-axial-momentum`) {#sec-ch07-axial}

### Summary

On the cubed sphere the momentum rows are covariant components in each panel's basis, and the finite-volume update
conserves them face by face only in that basis. The axial angular momentum (AAM) about the rotation axis is not one
of the rows, so a plain update lets it drift. The key `dynamics.conserve-axial-momentum` repairs this in two
levels. `transport` rewrites the AAM component of each cell's flux divergence as the divergence of face AAM
fluxes, so transport changes the global AAM only through physical boundary faces. `exact` adds the Coriolis torque
of the solver's dissipative lateral mass flux in the same flux form, and a closure that removes, once per stage, the
global AAM residual of the cell-form Coriolis force as one solid-body increment.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Keeps the global AAM about the $\Omega_1$ axis to round-off, @eq-ch07-axial-flux and @eq-ch07-axial-closure.

**Data.** Reads the face fluxes, the Coriolis force and the flux register's kept central flux; writes the momentum rows $m_2$, $m_3$.

**Placement.** `transport`: the divergence phase and the $x_1$ metric source of `HydroImpl::forward`. `exact`: also the pre-implicit Coriolis call, and the global phase after each stage.

**Activation.** `dynamics.conserve-axial-momentum`: `off` (default), `transport` or `exact`; acts on `gnomonic-equiangle` only.

**Guarantee / limits.** `transport` without rotation, and `exact`, keep the global AAM to $10^{-12}$ relative in the tests; with rotation `transport` leaves the exchange with the planetary AAM open.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch07-axial-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf k$ the rotation field about the $\Omega_1$ axis on the unit sphere, with $|\mathbf k|^2$ the squared cosine of the latitude;
$\mathbf K=r\mathbf k$; $s=r|\mathbf k|$ the distance from the axis [m]; $L$ the AAM of a set of cells
[$\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$]; $\mathcal A_i$ a target AAM rate of cell $i$ per volume; $A_f$ the area of face $f$;
$r_f$ the AAM radius of face $f$; $M_f$ the outward mass flux through face $f$ times $A_f$ [$\mathrm{kg\,s^{-1}}$];
$\mathcal Q$, $\mathcal J$ the closure's residual and moment of inertia; $w_2^{(s)}$ the stage weight of the increment
(@sec-ch09-rk).

### Derivation

**The AAM of the rows.** With $m_2$, $m_3$ the covariant momentum rows and $k^2$, $k^3$ the contravariant components of
$\mathbf k$, the AAM of a set of cells is

$$
L=\sum_iV_i\,r_i\,(k^2m_2+k^3m_3)_i=\sum_iV_i\,\mathbf K_i\cdot\mathbf m_i .
$$

**Transport in flux form.** The AAM rate of cell $i$ from the fluxes is the divergence of the face AAM fluxes
$A_f\,r_f\,\mathbf F_f\cdot\mathbf k_f$, with $\mathbf F_f$ the momentum flux of face $f$:

$$
\mathcal A_i=\frac{1}{V_i}\sum_{f\in\partial i}\pm A_f\,r_f\,\mathbf F_f\cdot\mathbf k_f ,
\qquad
r_f=\begin{cases}x_{1f} & x_1\text{ faces},\\[2pt]
\dfrac{2\,(r_+^3-r_-^3)}{3\,(r_+^2-r_-^2)} & x_2,\,x_3\text{ faces}.\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-ch07-axial-flux}

On a lateral face $r_f$ is the area-weighted radius, so $r_f\mathbf k_f$ is the face average of $\mathbf K$. Each face
value enters its two cells with opposite signs, so wherever $\mathbf F_f$ and $\mathbf k_f$ are single-valued the sum
$\sum_iV_i\mathcal A_i$ telescopes to the physical boundary faces. On an $x_1$ face $\mathbf K$ is tangent to the face,
so the pressure part of the flux carries no AAM.

**Setting the AAM component of a row pair.** Given a target $\mathcal A_i$, the code changes the rows
$(d_2,d_3)$ only along $\mathbf K$, the direction of a zonal acceleration, so that $\mathbf K\cdot\mathbf d=\mathcal A$:

$$
\lambda=\frac{\mathcal A-r\,(k^2d_2+k^3d_3)}{r^2|\mathbf k|^2},\qquad d_a\leftarrow d_a+\lambda\,r\,k_a ,
$$

which gives $r\,k^a(d_a+\lambda rk_a)=r\,k^ad_a+\lambda r^2|\mathbf k|^2=\mathcal A$. The component of the rows
across $\mathbf K$ is unchanged. A cell centred on the axis has $\mathbf K_i=0$ and holds no AAM; its target is handed
to its four lateral neighbours in equal shares, so the sum still telescopes.

**The Coriolis torque in flux form (`exact`).** The cell-form Coriolis force does no work but exchanges AAM with the
planetary AAM, $\Omega s^2$ per unit mass. A mass flux $M_f$ through a lateral face moves planetary AAM
$\Omega M_fs_f^2$; relative to the cell's own $\Omega s_c^2$ its torque is

$$
\mathcal A^{\mathrm{cor}}_i=-\frac{\Omega}{V_i}\sum_{f\in\partial i}M_f\,(s_f^2-s_{c,i}^2) .
$$

`exact` evaluates it on the dissipative part of the lateral mass flux, $M_f-M_f^{\mathrm{central}}$, where
$M^{\mathrm{central}}=\tfrac12(F(w_L)+F(w_R))$ is the solver's pre-limiter central flux kept in the flux register,
and adds it along $\mathbf K$ to the cell-form force. The $x_1$ faces are left out: in 3-D their exchange is carried by
the Coriolis rows that take $\rho w$ from the stage's $x_1$ mass transfer (@sec-ch07-coriolis).

**The closure (`exact`).** What remains is the residual of the cell-form force against the torque of the central
flux, summed over the whole mesh:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal Q&=\sum_iV_i\Big(\mathbf K_i\cdot\mathbf F^{\mathrm{cor}}_i-\mathcal A_i^{\mathrm{cor}}(M^{\mathrm{central}})\Big),
\qquad \mathcal J=\sum_iV_i\,\rho_i\,s_i^2 ,\\
\mathbf K_i\cdot\Delta\mathbf m_i&=-\,w_2^{(s)}\,\Delta t\,\frac{\mathcal Q}{\mathcal J}\,\rho_i\,s_i^2 ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch07-axial-closure}

a solid-body increment. Summing $V_i$ times the second line gives $\sum_iV_i\mathbf K_i\cdot\Delta\mathbf m_i=-w_2^{(s)}\Delta
t\,\mathcal Q$: the closure removes the residual exactly, and each block's share is $\mathcal J_b/\mathcal J$ of it.
$\mathcal Q$ is built from the Coriolis force and the mass fluxes only, so a physical torque (viscosity, a sponge,
a drag) is not part of it and is kept.

### Numerical method

Per stage, with `transport` or `exact` in force:

1. after the divergence, `AxialMomentum::flux_form` sets the $\mathbf K$ component of the momentum rows of `_div` to
   @eq-ch07-axial-flux from the $x_1$, $x_2$ and $x_3$ fluxes of the stage
   ({{< code src/forcing/axial_momentum.cpp AxialMomentum::flux_form >}});
2. `exact` only: `HydroImpl::forward` arms the torque for the pre-implicit Coriolis call, where `CoriolisImpl::add`
   calls `add_torque`, which adds $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{cor}}$ of the dissipative flux and records this block's
   $\{\mathcal Q_b,\mathcal J_b\}$ on the device; the torque is disarmed before the post-implicit call
   ({{< code src/forcing/axial_momentum.cpp AxialMomentum::add_torque >}});
3. in the post-implicit step, the $x_1$ metric source's $\mathbf K$ component is set so that the tangential momentum
   the implicit solve moved between two cells sits at the face radius (`x1_source`);
4. `exact` only, in the global phase after the blocks' stage: the partial sums of all blocks are added in one
   reduction, and every block applies @eq-ch07-axial-closure with the stage's $w_2$
   ({{< code src/forcing/axial_momentum.cpp AxialClosureFixer::apply >}}). A non-finite $\mathcal Q$ or
   $\mathcal J\le0$ is masked on the device and leaves the state unchanged. The increment is booked in the flux
   register as the fixer amount `aam.closure`.

`Mesh::forward` runs step 4 over its blocks; a single block run through `MeshBlockImpl::forward` runs it on its own.

**What switches it off.** The option does nothing on a grid other than `gnomonic-equiangle`. With a Coriolis force
that is not `type: xyz` with $\Omega_2=\Omega_3=0$ it warns once and stays off. `exact` is refused at setup
without `geometry.cells.interp_order: 4`, in FP32 or with `perturbation-flux`, and with a Riemann solver that
writes no central flux (allowed: `hllc`, `lmars`, `roe`, `shallow-roe`).

: Code map of the axial angular momentum. {#tbl-ch07-axial-code}

**The deck switch.** Under `dynamics`, set `conserve-axial-momentum` to `exact` (or `transport`); on a
`gnomonic-equiangle` grid with `geometry.cells.interp_order: 4`, and, if the deck has a Coriolis force, with
`forcing.coriolis` of `type: xyz` about $\Omega_1$ only. `transport` needs neither the interpolation order nor the
Coriolis form.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
1. **`transport` with rotation.** The Coriolis force stays in cell form and its exchange with the planetary AAM is
   left open; the absolute AAM is not exact. The test asks only that the drift be `GAIN` times below `off` at slow
   rotation.
2. **Cubed sphere only.** On every other grid the key is read and does nothing.
3. **The deck text and the code differ on viscosity.** The key's description in `hydro.yaml` says `exact` needs no
   `forcing.diffusion.nu_iso`; the constructor refuses no viscosity, and `ViscousTorque` runs `exact` with
   `nu_iso`. The code is what runs.
4. **`traditional: true`.** The Coriolis rows that carry the $x_1$ exchange are absent, so the $x_1$ part of the
   exchange is not closed by them.
5. **Not measured in a GCM configuration** at the pin; the tests are six-panel test decks and Williamson 2.
:::
